## Tours via Maipo Valley: wineries on Chile itineraries

[Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) lies near [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and is best known for red wines, particularly Cabernet Sauvignon. Visits introduce travelers to vineyards, winemaking, and different tasting formats. For someone already flying into Santiago, it is a way to add a meaningful gastronomic day without another flight across the country.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a visit to Maipo on the main itinerary. Some programs begin with wine and the capital; in others, the tasting is the finale to several weeks of travel or a visit to Easter Island. Choose according to the actual day-by-day sequence: the same valley can serve different purposes.

## Which programs feature Maipo as a separate stop?

| Program | Wine experience |
|---|---|
| [VIP Chile 5*](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) | Day 2, after Santiago |
| [Private Chile and Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) | Day 9, tasting in Maipo |
| [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) | Final day in Chile |

On [“VIP Chile 5*”](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/), a sightseeing tour through Santiago's historic center and modern neighborhoods is combined with a tasting in Maipo on Day 2. The itinerary then continues through Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and later to Patagonia. This sequence suits travelers who want to begin with the country's city history and wine, leaving nature destinations for subsequent days.

On the [private Chile and Easter Island journey](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/), the wine valley is scheduled for Day 9. After Rapa Nui's archaeological monuments, the tasting brings travelers back to central Chile. Here Maipo provides a separate, relaxed excursion day before the journey ends.

The [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) finishes its itinerary with Santiago and Maipo Valley. Before that, travelers explore Brazil, Argentina, Patagonia, and northern Chile. The wine stop offers a change of experience after longer nature excursions, but it is important to remember that it comes at the end of a multi-region journey.

## How a wine excursion works

Maipo's historic wine-growing areas lie in different parts of the valley. Chile's national tourism portal especially associates the region with Cabernet Sauvignon and describes visits to wineries, cellars, and tasting rooms. Producers differ in tour duration, wines served, food experiences, and booking rules. **The word “tasting” on an itinerary does not mean that you can visit any winery you choose or that dinner is included.**

Ada Tours also offers a standalone [Maipo Valley wine excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/). It is a useful reference for the subject, but each tour's own itinerary determines the winery, tasting selection, and additional services. If you are visiting for a particular wine or producer, clarify this before finalizing the day.

When comparing Maipo with [Casablanca Valley](/chile/place/casablanca-valley/) and [Colchagua](/chile/place/colchagua-valley/), start with the geography: Maipo combines naturally with Santiago, while Casablanca fits a trip toward the Pacific coast. Each valley has its own winemaking identity. Several names appearing on a route do not guarantee tastings in all those regions.

## What to check when choosing a wine tour

**Time during the day.** If Maipo is combined with a city tour, part of the day goes to monuments and the drive. That format suits a first introduction to Chilean wine. A deeper look at a winery requires a separate program with a confirmed amount of visiting time.

**Transport and tastings.** Arrange a car and the return to Santiago beforehand: you must not drive after wine tasting. If an international flight is scheduled for the same day, allow sufficient time for the winery's location and road conditions. Chile's tourism portal recommends booking winery visits in advance, particularly on busy dates.

**Season.** Wineries can be visited at different times of year, but the experience changes. Harvest season may bring special events, while in other months the focus shifts to cellars and tasting finished wines. A particular event, seasonal dinner, or participation in harvesting grapes is not automatically part of the chosen tour.

If you want to build a journey mainly around food and wine, compare [Chile food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) and the general [Chile tour selection](/chile/tour/). A gastronomic interest may be the purpose of the whole trip or one day within a wider itinerary; these are different travel goals.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Maipo

### Can I visit Maipo Valley on a day trip from Santiago?

Yes. This is a common format. A winery visit and return to the capital can fit into one excursion day, with the exact duration depending on the estate and selected activities.

### Do all the tours include tastings and lunch?

Tastings are listed on the wine days described, but inclusions and itinerary details differ. Lunch, a particular number of wines, access to a specific winery, and private service cannot be assumed from the valley's name.

### Is it better to put Maipo at the beginning or end of the trip?

Both work: on the [VIP Chile route](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/), it comes early, while on the [Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) it is part of the finale. Choose the wine day's position based on flights and how demanding the preceding days have been.

### How does Maipo differ from Casablanca?

Maipo is known for red grape varieties, especially Cabernet Sauvignon, and its proximity to Santiago. [Casablanca](/chile/place/casablanca-valley/) has cooler growing conditions on the route to the ocean. For a particular wine or producer, select a suitable specific route rather than relying on the generic description “wine tour.”

## Marble Caves in Chile: boat, kayak, and the best time to visit

**The Marble Caves (Capillas de Mármol) are worth visiting for their extraordinary stone arches and reflections of turquoise water, but they can only be seen from the lake.** They are a distinctive natural attraction of the Aysén Region in Chilean Patagonia. Over thousands of years, water has worn away the pale rock, creating curved vaults and galleries. The color of the stone and water changes with the light, weather, and position of your boat.

Two different places are involved in the journey: [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) is the natural setting, while [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) is the main starting point for excursions on the water. Because the caves lie on the lake, a roadside stop along Carretera Austral is not a substitute for visiting them.

## Boat or kayak: which experience should you choose?

Chile's tourism portal describes two common options. A **motorboat** carries travelers along the water route to see the arches from onboard, while a **kayak** brings you closer to the rock formations but requires physical fitness and suitable conditions on the lake.

| Format | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Motorboat | Less physical exertion |
| Kayak | Paddling independently, closer to the water |

For kayaking, consider not only the trip's duration but also your ability to paddle if the wind changes. On boat excursions, too, you must follow the crew's instructions and wear a life jacket. Whether you can enter individual grottoes depends on water levels and the vessel's dimensions. **Entering every cave cannot be promised in advance:** the operator makes the safe decision on site.

Choose an outing on more than the photographs. Ask about the departure point, vessel type, length of time on the lake, age limits and physical requirements, and cancellation rules in bad weather.

## When to visit Capillas de Mármol

Chile's official tourism portal identifies **November to March** as the most popular period. During Patagonian summer, daylight hours are usually longer and conditions are often more suitable for excursions. This does not mean the lake is always calm: wind and waves can disrupt plans even at the height of the season.

Water level affects access to the arches. In different months, and after snowmelt, narrow passages can be partly filled with water. Higher water does not necessarily spoil the views of the outer arches or photographs, but the actual excursion may differ from promotional images.

The practical conclusion: if you are traveling specifically for the caves, **allow some flexibility in your schedule**, especially when the trip includes a long road journey through Patagonia. Booking a single short time slot with no opportunity to reschedule increases the risk of missing the boat trip because of wind.

## How to get to Puerto Río Tranquilo

The village stands on the Chilean shore of General Carrera Lake, beside the Carretera Austral highway. The road from Coyhaique runs through Aysén, with some gravel stretches. Actual journey time depends on the road's condition, weather, and stops.

[Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) makes a useful overnight base if you plan excursions on the water. This avoids tying a boat departure to the fixed timing of another long drive. On our longer [Chile tours](/chile/tour/), check whether a boat excursion is actually included or the program mentions only a stop on the lake's shore.

General Carrera Lake spans parts of Chile and Argentina; on the Argentine side it is known as Lake Buenos Aires. Do not confuse a road border crossing with the excursion itself: the main departure point for Capillas de Mármol is on the Chilean side.

## What to pack and how to take photographs

Even in summer, it may feel colder on the lake than in the village. Bring windproof clothing, a waterproof layer or protection for belongings against spray, nonslip footwear, and a secure strap for your camera. Use the safety equipment required by the operator.

In bright sunshine, contrast between shaded recesses and light-colored water can be strong. Try different angles rather than relying on a single photograph. Safety aboard matters more than a picture: do not lean over the edge or move around without permission as the boat approaches the rock arches.

The Marble Caves complement other natural experiences in Patagonia, but a visit depends on weather and access to water transport. To compare nature-focused trips, see our [Wildlife and Nature section](/interests/wildlife/) and [Chile guide](/chile/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Marble Caves

### Can I walk to the Marble Caves?

No. A normal tourist visit involves going out on the water. The route starts near [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) on [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/).

### Can I enter the marble arches?

Sometimes, but only with safe water levels and suitable weather. The operator decides, and the actual route may differ from what was planned.

### Is it worth visiting in winter?

Excursions may be possible outside summer, but weather and operator schedules restrict availability. November to March is the more popular period for planning.

### Which is better: a kayak or a motorboat?

A kayak requires paddling and physical fitness. A motorboat is generally more accessible to travelers without that experience. Choose according to weather, safety, and the actual excursion arrangements.

## Tours to the Marble Caves in Chile: what should you choose?

The [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) lie on [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) in Chilean Patagonia. Water has carved arches, recesses, and grottoes into the marble, best viewed from a boat. Rock colors and reflections depend on light and lake conditions; the crew determines whether individual arches can be approached on the day.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the Marble Caves on the main itinerary. A short tour focuses on the Aysén Region; other programs combine it with the Atacama Desert or several South American countries. The main decision is **how much time you want to spend on this remote part of Carretera Austral for a boat ride and other Patagonian attractions**.

## Four current formats

| Program | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Marble Caves and San Rafael: 3 days](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) | Lake, boats, and glacier |
| [Chile's Hidden Treasures: 9 days](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) | Atacama and Patagonia |
| [Bolivia and Chile: 16 days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) | Uyuni, Atacama, and Aysén |
| [Grand South America: 33 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) | Peru, Bolivia, and Chile |

**Three days in Aysén.** The [“Marble Caves and San Rafael Glacier” itinerary](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) begins with arrival in Balmaceda and a drive to [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/). Day 2 is devoted to a separate excursion toward [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/), and the morning of Day 3 includes a private boat to the Marble Caves. The group then drives toward Balmaceda. Despite its short duration, the program includes several long transfers.

**Nine days in Chile.** [“Chile's Hidden Treasures”](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) begins in Santiago and the Atacama, followed by a flight to Aysén. Day 6 includes a journey to San Rafael, while Day 7 features a morning boat excursion to the Marble Caves, followed by a road transfer and a flight south toward Puerto Natales. This route suits travelers seeking contrasting regions of one country, but the schedule is busy.

**Bolivia and Chile.** The [16-day journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) includes the Uyuni Salt Flat and Altiplano lagoons, then the Atacama, southern Chilean mountains, and the General Carrera area. The itinerary includes both a trip to San Rafael and a visit to the Marble Caves. Combining them means preparing for very different elevations and weather.

**Grand continental journey.** On the [33-day tour through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), the Marble Caves come near the end of the trip. It is designed for travelers who want to include Aysén within a longer journey across other regions rather than visit Patagonia only for the lake.

## How to reach the caves

The usual route leads through [Balmaceda Airport](/chile/place/balmaceda/) to [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) via [Carretera Austral](/chile/place/carretera-austral/). Boats depart from the village to the marble formations on the lake. This is different from exploring a cave on foot: the principal views are from the water.

Chile's official tourism portal describes boat trips from Puerto Río Tranquilo and the need to arrange departures in advance. The road leg cannot be reduced to the distance on a map: weather, road surfaces, flight timetables, and stops among the mountains affect the actual journey time. Allowing a sensible margin is especially important when a boat trip and a flight fall on the same day.

On Ada Tours itineraries, the Marble Caves are often combined with another water-based experience: [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/). They are, however, **two separate excursions**. The caves lie on General Carrera Lake, while San Rafael is reached through Exploradores Valley and the glacial lagoon. Even when both are on the same tour, they normally occupy different days.

## What affects the experience and safety?

Wind and waves are crucial on the lake. They determine whether the boat can depart and how closely it may approach individual grottoes. The brightness of water and reflections also changes with the light, so the exact “blue walls in the photograph” cannot be guaranteed. Choose a program with a sensible time margin and remember that every planned boat trip depends on weather.

For an excursion, bring waterproof outerwear, a warm layer, and protection for your phone or camera. Even in warmer months, an open boat can feel colder than the shore. Local operators decide on routing and whether departure is safe. If you have difficulty boarding boats or are very susceptible to seasickness, discuss the format beforehand.

For a separate short visit, examine the [three-day itinerary](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) and its day-by-day sequence. To add other regions, compare the [nine-day Chile route](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) with the [16-day Bolivia and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). The [General Carrera Lake page](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) provides more information about the place itself; here the question is which tour to choose.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to the Marble Caves

### Can I see the caves in one day?

If you are already in Puerto Río Tranquilo, the boat excursion occupies part of a day. Reaching the area from another region via Balmaceda and Carretera Austral takes additional time. That is why Ada Tours' short program allocates three days to Aysén.

### Are the caves and San Rafael Glacier a single excursion?

No. They are separate natural attractions with different water routes. On the [three-day program](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/), Day 2 is devoted to the glacier, and the morning of Day 3 to the caves.

### Do boats go out in strong winds?

Departure depends on conditions and the local operator's decision. If the excursion cannot go ahead, the next steps depend on the circumstances and terms of your specific tour; entry into the grottoes cannot be guaranteed in advance.

### Which tour is best if I only want Patagonia?

For a focused introduction to Aysén, choose the [three-day itinerary](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/). To also see the desert and Torres del Paine, compare [“Chile's Hidden Treasures”](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) by its flights and time allocated to each region.

## Marta Island: sea lions in the Strait of Magellan

Marta Island (Isla Marta) lies in the Strait of Magellan in southern [Chile](/chile/), near Magdalena Island. Its rocky shores are home to large groups of sea lions and seabirds. Tourists observe these animals **from a boat** as marine excursions follow the coast, allowing visitors to see the colonies without disturbing them.

It is a distinct natural destination that is easy to confuse with neighboring Magdalena. Both islands feature on boat trips from [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/), but their main wildlife and the arrangements for seeing it differ.

## How Marta Island differs from Magdalena Island

On Magdalena, travelers primarily come to see **Magellanic penguins**. When landing is permitted, visitors follow a marked path through their nesting areas. Marta, by contrast, is particularly known for **South American sea lion colonies**: according to the official Chile Travel portal, they are observed from the deck. Standard tourist excursions do not include landing on Marta.

A single boat trip can therefore reveal two different types of animal and two different ways of observing them. On Magdalena, staying on the marked trail and keeping your distance from the birds is essential; near Marta, observation takes place from the water, with the captain choosing a safe distance from the rocks.

### Sea lions and seabirds

On Marta's shores, sea lions rest in groups, sometimes enter the water, and interact with one another. Their calls may be heard before the boat approaches close enough for a clear view. Cormorants and other seabirds also inhabit the area. Wildlife watching is more enjoyable in calm weather, when the vessel can safely maintain its course along the shore.

A lens with some zoom is useful for photography. Avoid noise and do not ask the captain to approach dangerously close to rocks. Feeding wildlife or trying to attract animals to the boat runs counter to the principles of responsible nature excursions.

## How a trip from Punta Arenas works

The main departure city is Punta Arenas, on the shore of the strait. Travelers go to the designated pier, receive a safety briefing, and board an authorized vessel. Typical excursions to Los Pingüinos Natural Monument take several hours; Chile's official tourism portal offers **4–6 hours** as an approximate duration for the full outing, including sailing and scheduled stops.

This is an indicative format for routes in the area, not an exact duration promised for every trip to Marta. Vessels, departure piers, and the sequence of islands vary. On some days, conditions permit viewing Marta but prevent landing on Magdalena, or vice versa.

Some excursions include both islands, while others concentrate on one part of the strait. Before booking, distinguish **“approaching an island”** from **“landing on an island.”**

## When to see the wildlife and how weather affects trips

Trips to the island colonies are particularly popular in the warmer Southern Hemisphere months, during Magdalena's visiting season. Actual sailing dates depend on the operator, protected-area rules, and sea conditions. Winds in the Strait of Magellan can be strong even on sunny days.

Pack windproof and waterproof clothing, a warm hat, nonslip footwear, and protection for electronic equipment from salt spray. If you are prone to seasickness, allow for a lengthy stretch at sea. Operators may cancel or reschedule departures when the forecast is unfavorable, so it is better not to leave the island trip until the last few hours before a flight.

## Combining Marta Island with Patagonia

A boat excursion complements the urban attractions of Punta Arenas and nature itineraries in [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). In the mountains, you may see guanacos, lakes, and glaciers; in the Strait of Magellan, marine mammal and bird colonies. Such a combination usually requires several days and accommodation in different areas.

Our [“Luxury Patagonia: 10-Day VIP Tour of Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/) includes Marta Island. Check the whole itinerary: time on the water, road transfers, other stops, and weather-related possibilities depend on the specific day. More southern Chile options are available in the [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Marta Island

### Can I land on Marta Island?

On ordinary tourist trips, sea lions are observed **from the vessel**, without landing. Magdalena Island offers a different format, with a permitted walk along a trail.

### Are there penguins on Marta Island?

The main focus of the Marta excursion is sea lions. Visitors usually choose neighboring Magdalena to watch Magellanic penguins.

### Can I see sea lions year-round?

The animals live in the strait, but the availability of tourist boat trips depends on seasonal rules and weather. Sightings on a particular day cannot be guaranteed.

### Where do the boats depart?

Usually from Punta Arenas. Confirm the exact boarding point, type of vessel, and return time for the chosen excursion.

[Marta Island](/chile/place/marta-island-strait-of-magellan/) lies in the Strait of Magellan near [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/). Its rocky coast is known for colonies of sea lions and seabirds. The island is reached by sea, and animals are watched from the vessel; **landing on Marta itself is not part of the confirmed program**.

Sailing is scheduled for Day 8, after travel through Argentine and Chilean Patagonia. A flight to Santiago follows. Marta Island is part of a longer journey here, not a standalone multi-day cruise.

## What happens on the sailing day?

The excursion combines two different islands. Magdalena is known for Magellanic penguins, while Marta is associated with sea lions. Near Marta, visitors observe the animals **from the boat, without going ashore**. This is a crucial distinction when choosing a journey: walking among animals on Marta is not included.

During the voyage, you see shores, rocks, and the open waters of the strait. Wildlife sightings depend on weather, distance from shore, and the animals' behavior. No particular number of encounters or close approach of sea lions to the vessel can be guaranteed. Travelers experience southern Chile's marine nature after several days devoted to glaciers and mountains.

If wildlife is your main goal, compare this itinerary with [wildlife-watching journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/). A boat trip to the islands differs from wildlife observation in national parks: conditions depend on navigation, rather than the length of a walking trail.

## Combining Marta Island and Patagonia

Before the sailing day on the 10-day trip, the itinerary includes [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Perito Moreno Glacier, and the Chilean [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine area](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Punta Arenas is the departure point for the islands and the onward flight to northern Chile.

This suits travelers interested in both glacial and mountain scenery and marine wildlife. When comparing tours, check **whether the actual sailing to Marta Island is included**, how much time is allocated to the outing, and where the next overnight stay takes place. Mentioning Punta Arenas alone does not mean that a trip to the islands has already been paid for.

## Weather and preparation for sailing

Strong winds can quickly alter conditions on the Strait of Magellan. Bring a waterproof, windproof jacket, warm layers, and closed-toe shoes with nonslip soles. A zoom lens helps with photography from the boat.

Sailing depends on wind and waves, and the operator decides whether navigation is safe. This matters especially when a flight is scheduled for the following day. Ada Tours helps coordinate the boat excursion with the rest of the itinerary and clarify practical arrangements.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Marta Island

### Can I land on Marta Island?

Not on the tour described: the sea lions are observed from the vessel. Whether landing on neighboring Magdalena is possible is confirmed for the particular sailing.

### How does Marta differ from Magdalena?

Sea lions are the main attraction at Marta; Magellanic penguins are the focus at Magdalena. Weather and animal behavior affect observations at both islands.

### Is the trip suitable for photography?

Yes, if you are happy to photograph animals from onboard. Close proximity to the wildlife and calm seas cannot be promised in advance.
